chapters.title: The Characters of the Story
chapters.sourcePressure: introduces System 1 and System 2 as fast intuitive suggestion and slow deliberate checking; the mind feels unified even though these modes play different roles
chapters.coreMove: separate the first answer your mind offers from the slower act of endorsing it
chapters.commonMisread: turning the two systems into cartoon brain parts or treating slow thought as always better

chapters.title: Attention and Effort
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that deliberate thought depends on limited attention and effort that can be stretched, spent, or overloaded
chapters.coreMove: notice when a judgment requires scarce attention before you trust the first fluent answer
chapters.commonMisread: calling attention a moral virtue instead of a limited cognitive budget

chapters.title: The Lazy Controller
chapters.sourcePressure: argues that System 2 often accepts System 1 suggestions instead of auditing them closely because effort is costly
chapters.coreMove: catch the moment when your inner reviewer rubber-stamps an easy answer
chapters.commonMisread: framing laziness as stupidity rather than an effort-saving default

chapters.title: The Associative Machine
chapters.sourcePressure: explains how associative memory links ideas quickly and shapes what feels available, threatening, or normal
chapters.coreMove: trace a judgment back to the cue-chain that activated it before you treat it as independent evidence
chapters.commonMisread: reducing association to random word games rather than a mechanism that steers perception

chapters.title: Cognitive Ease
chapters.sourcePressure: shows how fluency, familiarity, and ease make claims feel truer and safer than they deserve
chapters.coreMove: discount the extra credibility that comes only from a claim feeling easy to process
chapters.commonMisread: equating ease with comfort or relaxation instead of truth-feeling

chapters.title: Norms, Surprises, and Causes
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that the mind notices broken norms quickly and rushes to causal stories that restore order
chapters.coreMove: pause after surprise and separate the violated expectation from the cause you are tempted to invent
chapters.commonMisread: treating surprise as curiosity only, rather than a trigger for causal overreach

chapters.title: A Machine for Jumping to Conclusions
chapters.sourcePressure: describes the mind as a coherence engine that forms conclusions from thin evidence and treats what is visible as enough
chapters.coreMove: ask what evidence is absent before letting a coherent story become your verdict
chapters.commonMisread: making this about rushing in general instead of WYSIATI and missing evidence

chapters.title: How Judgments Happen
chapters.sourcePressure: tracks how quick judgments borrow intensity, substitute dimensions, and convert vague questions into simpler impressions
chapters.coreMove: identify the hidden scale your mind used when it answered a vague question quickly
chapters.commonMisread: summarizing judgment as pure emotion instead of intensity-matching and dimension substitution

chapters.title: Answering an Easier Question
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that hard questions are often answered by easier ones without the swap being noticed
chapters.coreMove: name the question you actually answered and compare it with the question you were asked
chapters.commonMisread: turning substitution into deliberate evasion rather than an unnoticed mental shortcut

chapters.title: The Law of Small Numbers
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that people expect stable patterns from samples far too small to justify confidence
chapters.coreMove: withhold pattern claims until the sample is large enough to deserve them
chapters.commonMisread: calling every small sample useless instead of seeing how noise masquerades as signal

chapters.title: Anchors
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that irrelevant starting points pull estimates and negotiations toward themselves
chapters.coreMove: strip out the first number in the room before you make your own estimate
chapters.commonMisread: limiting anchoring to price negotiation rather than any starting value that pulls judgment

chapters.title: The Science of Availability
chapters.sourcePressure: explains that ease of recall is often mistaken for frequency, importance, or probability
chapters.coreMove: separate how easily examples come to mind from how often the event actually happens
chapters.commonMisread: treating availability as mere media influence instead of memory fluency used as evidence

chapters.title: Availability, Emotion, and Risk
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that vivid emotion amplifies availability and bends judgments about danger and safety
chapters.coreMove: measure the risk after naming the image or feeling that made it loom larger
chapters.commonMisread: telling readers to ignore fear instead of calibrating vivid risk against frequency

chapters.title: Tom W's Specialty
chapters.sourcePressure: uses representativeness to show how stereotype fit can overpower base rates
chapters.coreMove: put the base rate back on the table before a vivid description sorts someone into a category
chapters.commonMisread: turning representativeness into prejudice alone instead of stereotype fit overpowering probability

chapters.title: Linda: Less Is More
chapters.sourcePressure: uses the conjunction fallacy to show that richer stories can feel more probable than broader truths
chapters.coreMove: prefer the broader category when added detail makes a story sound better but mathematically narrower
chapters.commonMisread: making this about gullibility instead of the probability cost of extra detail

chapters.title: Causes Trump Statistics
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that causal stories and stereotypes often overpower clean statistical reasoning
chapters.coreMove: notice when a causal explanation has displaced the distribution it was supposed to update
chapters.commonMisread: framing statistics as always cold and stories as always wrong

chapters.title: Regression to the Mean
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that extreme outcomes are often followed by more ordinary ones without praise or blame causing the shift
chapters.coreMove: treat the rebound from an extreme result as regression before assigning credit or blame
chapters.commonMisread: using regression as a synonym for decline instead of return toward average after extremity

chapters.title: Taming Intuitive Predictions
chapters.sourcePressure: shows how intuitive forecasts improve when base rates and regression are given explicit weight
chapters.coreMove: shrink an intuitive forecast toward the base rate before acting on it
chapters.commonMisread: telling readers to abandon intuition instead of correcting it with base rates and regression

chapters.title: The Illusion of Understanding
chapters.sourcePressure: shows how coherent stories about the past create an exaggerated sense that the world was predictable all along
chapters.coreMove: break a neat hindsight story by restoring the alternatives and luck it erased
chapters.commonMisread: calling every success story fake instead of showing how coherence hides uncertainty

chapters.title: The Illusion of Validity
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that strong confidence in judgment can survive even when predictive validity is weak
chapters.coreMove: downgrade confidence when the task gives coherent impressions but weak predictive feedback
chapters.commonMisread: treating confidence as arrogance only instead of a feeling produced by coherence

chapters.title: Intuitions vs. Formulas
chapters.sourcePressure: argues that simple formulas often outperform expert judgment in stable prediction tasks
chapters.coreMove: use a consistent rule when prediction conditions are stable enough for noise to hurt more than nuance helps
chapters.commonMisread: presenting formulas as magic or experts as useless across all settings

chapters.title: Expert Intuition: When Can We Trust It?
chapters.sourcePressure: defines the conditions under which expert intuition deserves trust and when it does not
chapters.coreMove: grant intuition only when the environment is regular and feedback has trained it
chapters.commonMisread: trusting credentials or dismissing expertise without checking learning conditions

chapters.title: The Outside View
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that planning improves when you use reference classes instead of relying on the inside view
chapters.coreMove: anchor a plan in comparable completed cases before adjusting for your own details
chapters.commonMisread: treating the outside view as pessimism rather than reference-class discipline

chapters.title: The Engine of Capitalism
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that optimism and overconfidence create energy for risk taking even while they also create waste and failure
chapters.coreMove: use optimism for action while forcing the forecast through independent survival odds
chapters.commonMisread: celebrating optimism or condemning entrepreneurship instead of holding the double effect

chapters.title: Bernoulli's Errors
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that classical utility theory misses how people evaluate gains and losses relative to a reference point
chapters.coreMove: evaluate a choice from the reference point the person actually feels, not only from final wealth
chapters.commonMisread: reducing this to money math instead of reference-dependent experience

chapters.title: Prospect Theory
chapters.sourcePressure: introduces prospect theory as a better account of how people value gains, losses, and certainty
chapters.coreMove: read a decision by its reference point, loss curve, and probability weighting instead of by final outcome alone
chapters.commonMisread: using prospect theory as a vague label for risk aversion

chapters.title: The Endowment Effect
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that ownership changes value and makes people demand more to give something up than to acquire it
chapters.coreMove: notice when ownership has turned a neutral trade into a felt loss
chapters.commonMisread: making this about greed or sentimental attachment only

chapters.title: Bad Events
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that bad events weigh more heavily than equally sized good events across attention, motivation, and choice
chapters.coreMove: give losses extra weight in your forecast because people respond to them more fiercely than to equal gains
chapters.commonMisread: turning negativity bias into pessimism rather than asymmetric psychological weight

chapters.title: The Fourfold Pattern
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that risk preferences flip depending on whether outcomes are framed as gains or losses and as likely or unlikely
chapters.coreMove: classify a gamble by gain or loss and high or low probability before predicting risk appetite
chapters.commonMisread: saying people are simply risk-averse or risk-seeking

chapters.title: Rare Events
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that rare events are overweighted in description and often neglected in experience until they strike
chapters.coreMove: ask whether you learned the risk from a description or from experience before judging how much it weighs
chapters.commonMisread: treating rare events as always exaggerated or always ignored

chapters.title: Risk Policies
chapters.sourcePressure: argues that broad risk policies beat one-off choices because narrow framing invites inconsistency
chapters.coreMove: replace isolated risk decisions with a standing policy that sees the whole portfolio
chapters.commonMisread: framing this as courage to take risks rather than broad framing and consistency

chapters.title: Keeping Score
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that mental accounting tracks gains and losses in separate ledgers instead of one clean total
chapters.coreMove: find the mental account that is driving the feeling before accepting the choice it produces
chapters.commonMisread: equating mental accounting with ordinary budgeting

chapters.title: Reversals
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that preferences can reverse when options are compared jointly instead of separately
chapters.coreMove: test a preference in both single and joint evaluation before trusting it
chapters.commonMisread: calling reversals inconsistency only instead of seeing evaluation mode change salience

chapters.title: Frames and Reality
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that wording and framing change decisions even when the underlying outcomes stay the same
chapters.coreMove: translate a framed choice into its equivalent wording before deciding
chapters.commonMisread: treating framing as mere spin rather than equivalent realities feeling different

chapters.title: Two Selves
chapters.sourcePressure: introduces the experiencing self and the remembering self as partly different judges of life
chapters.coreMove: ask whether you are optimizing the lived moment or the memory that will later judge it
chapters.commonMisread: splitting the self into therapy personas instead of two evaluative standpoints

chapters.title: Life as a Story
chapters.sourcePressure: shows that remembered lives are shaped by peaks and endings more than by duration
chapters.coreMove: design and judge experiences knowing the remembered story will overweight peaks and endings
chapters.commonMisread: telling readers memories are false instead of showing narrative compression

chapters.title: Experienced Well-Being
chapters.sourcePressure: argues that well-being should be measured in lived time as well as in remembered judgment
chapters.coreMove: sample how time actually feels before accepting a global life rating
chapters.commonMisread: turning well-being into happiness slogans instead of measurement of lived episodes

chapters.title: Thinking About Life
chapters.sourcePressure: shows how life satisfaction is vulnerable to focusing illusions and conflict between happiness, memory, and meaning
chapters.coreMove: defuse the focusing illusion before one salient fact stands in for your whole life
chapters.commonMisread: making this a generic happiness finale instead of showing attention distorts life judgment
